learningGoals: Expand vocabulary related to weather, the sky, and nature. 🌦️
Use imagination to describe the shapes and movements of clouds. 🦄
Identify basic colors and textures associated with the sky (white, soft, blue, dark). 🎨
Read poetic or descriptive sentences with expression and rhythm. 🎭
Develop observational skills by looking at the natural world. 🔭
conversationStarters: Have you ever seen a cloud that looked like a funny animal? What was it? 🦕
Where do you think the clouds go when the wind blows them away? 🌬️
Do you prefer sunny days with white fluffy clouds or rainy days with dark clouds? Why? ☔
teachingTips: Spend five minutes outside or looking out a window just watching the clouds move. 🪟
Encourage the use of descriptive adjectives. Ask, 'Is that cloud fluffy, flat, dark, or bright?' 🗣️
Link the weather to feelings. Talk about how a sunny sky or a rainy day makes them feel. 😊
Read the chapter together outdoors if the weather permits, making real-world connections. 🌳
Practice the 'cl' sound for 'cloud' and 'clean', and the 'sk' sound for 'sky'. 🔤

funActivities.title: Cotton Ball Cloud Art ☁️
funActivities.description: Give your child a blue piece of paper, some glue, and cotton balls. Ask them to stretch and glue the cotton to create their own cloud shapes, then write what shape it is.

funActivities.title: Cloud Shape Story 📖
funActivities.description: Look at the sky together. Pick a cloud shape and take turns making up a short, funny story about the 'cloud animal' you see.

funActivities.title: Daily Weather Chart 📅
funActivities.description: Create a weekly chart. Every morning, have your child draw the current weather (sun, clouds, rain) and write the English word next to it.
